Combat Resupply (in the field or at base)

In this video, Brent0331 goes over the concept of how his unit was using combat resupplies to reload mags in order to get back into the fight. He mostly goes over how these things work in the military, involving getting the shipment of supplies, getting ammo on stripper clips and using them to quickly reload your mags. He also goes into positioning ammo for reloading machine guns and things like that.

The lesson I'd like to go over with this one is that in a civilian sense, you can still use this concept for yourself. For example, I've got 2 separate plate carriers, one for an AK loadout and one for an AR loadout. In order to supplement this, I've got 2 separate ammo cans that each are filled up with loaded mags for each loadout. One ammo can has 6+ loaded AK mags, and one ammo can has 7+ loaded AR mags.

The point from this is that while you might have 6+ mags on your loadout, if any of your mags run dry, you really don't want to have to manually reload them in the field or in the back of your truck or anything like that. Get a weatherproof ammo can and fill it with loaded mags and keep it in the back of your truck during field operations or training, so that when your mags start to run dry you can just replace them with fully loaded mags in seconds and get back to work.

TL;DR - keep an ammo can full of loaded mags when you oper8e so when you have empty mags, you can just replace them with loaded mags and get back to work.
